facts.statement: The species was first described in 1940 by Charles Mortram Sternberg as Chasmosaurus russelli.
facts.quote: It was first named in 1940 by Charles Mortram Sternberg as a species of the genus Chasmosaurus and given the name Chasmosaurus russelli.

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Holmes, Mallon, Ryan, and Evans reprepared the holotype to clarify anatomy obscured by plaster reconstruction.
facts.quote: In 2026, a study by Robert B. Holmes, Jordan C. Mallon, Michael J. Ryan, and David C. Evans reevaluated the holotype and reprepared it to clarify the anatomy obscured by plaster reconstruction.

facts.statement: The partial parietal TMP 2013.019.0038 was recognized as belonging to the species in addition to the holotype.
facts.quote: In addition to the holotype, they recognized the partial parietal TMP 2013.019.0038 as belonging to the species.

facts.statement: Cryptarcus is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from the middle Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous found in Alberta.
facts.quote: Cryptarcus (meaning "hidden arch") is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur found in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, dating to the middle Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The skull is distinguished by a deep embayment on the back of the parietal frill and dome-shaped ornamentation along the edge of this embayment.
facts.quote: Amongst other traits of the skull, it can be distinguished by the deep embayment on the back of its parietal frill and the dome-shape of the ornamentation along the edge of this embayment.

facts.statement: Cryptarcus is a chasmosaurine ceratopsid that was established as a new genus for Chasmosaurus russelli.
facts.quote: A chasmosaurine ceratopsid; a new genus for "Chasmosaurus" russelli Sternberg (1940).

facts.statement: Its relationships are uncertain, but it may be more closely related to Utahceratops and Pentaceratops than to Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: While its relationships remain uncertain, it may be more closely related to animals such as Utahceratops and Pentaceratops rather than Chasmosaurus.

facts.statement: Cryptarcus lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) period.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Campanian)

facts.statement: The type locality of Cryptarcus is the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: Type locality: Dinosaur Park Formation

facts.statement: Cryptarcus fossils have been found in Canada.
facts.quote: Country: Canada

facts.statement: Cryptarcus fossils have been found in the region of Alberta.
facts.quote: Region: Alberta

facts.statement: It was previously debated that Chasmosaurus russelli came from lower layers of the Dinosaur Park Formation while C. belli came from upper layers, but this was later challenged.
facts.quote: Ostensibly, C. russelli was found in the lower layers of the Dinosaur Park Formation (making it older in geologic time), whereas those belonging to C. belli were from the upper layers of the formation.

facts.statement: Rediscovery of the holotype quarry revealed it to be from a high layer of the Dinosaur Park Formation, contradicting earlier assumptions.
facts.quote: Furthermore, rediscovery of the quarry where Sternberg discovered the holotype revealed it to be from a high layer of the Dinosaur Park Formation.

facts.statement: In 2010, Nick Longrich argued that many specimens referred to C. russelli represented Mojoceratops perifania, but this view was rejected by most researchers.
facts.quote: In 2010 Nick Longrich argued many of the specimens referred to C. russelli actually represented a new genus and species, Mojoceratops perifania, but this was rejected by most other researchers.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that definitive classification of chasmosaurs is difficult and that Cryptarcus might later be associated with another genus due to the lack of a definite link to Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: They noted that ongoing issues in the taxonomy of chasmosaurs made definitive classification difficult, and noted it was possible Cryptarcus may later become associated with another genus, the lack of any definite link to Chasmosaurus made it most responsible to give it a distinct genus.

facts.statement: Cryptarcus was a large, four-legged plant-eating dinosaur with a massive skull.
facts.quote: As a chasmosaurine ceratopsid, Cryptarcus would have been a large, quadrupedal herbivore with a massive skull.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Cryptarcus measures approximately 94 centimeters in length, but the rest of its skeleton is unknown.
facts.quote: The holotype skull of Cryptarcus is around 94 cm long, while the rest of the skeleton remains unknown.

facts.statement: The frill of Cryptarcus is about 120% of the length of the rest of the skull.
facts.quote: The parietosquamosal frill measures around 120% of the length of the rest of the skull.

facts.statement: Each squamosal bone of Cryptarcus bears eight episquamosals.
facts.quote: Each squamosal bears eight episquamosals.

facts.statement: Cryptarcus possesses only three epiparietal bones.
facts.quote: Only three epiparietals are present.

facts.statement: Taxonomic revisions found that the holotype of Cryptarcus cannot be definitively resolved as closer to either Chasmosaurus or Pentaceratops, with alternative methods supporting both possibilities.
facts.quote: Revision of the material and taxonomy of Cryptarcus found that CMN 8800 was not able to be resolved as closer to either Chasmosaurus or Pentaceratops, with alternative methodologies finding both options possible.

facts.statement: A 2026 reassessment by Holmes and colleagues produced phylogenetic results based on iterations with and without weighting.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic results following the reassessment of Holmes and colleagues (2026) are shown below, based on Iterations 1 and 2 (no weighting).

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses yield conflicting results, with some iterations placing Cryptarcus closer to Pentaceratops and others placing it closer to Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: Iterations 3 and 5 (k = 3) recovered Cryptarcus in an unresolved polytomy with Agujaceratops spp., more closely related to Pentaceratops than Chasmosaurus, while Iterations 4 and 6 (k = 12) recovered it closer to Chasmosaurus than Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: The genus Cryptarcus was established in 2026 by Holmes, Mallon, Ryan, and Evans in the Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences.
facts.quote: Journal: Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences Year: 2026 Authors: Robert B. Holmes, Jordan C. Mallon, Michael J. Ryan, David C. Evans

facts.statement: Recent hypotheses suggesting an evolutionary trend from Cryptarcus russelli through Pentaceratops to produce Terminocavus are not supported by the phylogenetic analysis presented in this study.
